sehemu: Part VII: Special Constitutional Court of the United Republic
jina: Procedure at sittings of the Special Constitutional Court
maudhui: (1) The Special Constitutional Court shall sit only when there is a matter to be heard and shall hold its sittings at such place as may be determined in accordance with the procedure applicable to matters before the Court. (2) The quorum at every sitting of the Special Constitutional Court shall be all its members; where any member is absent or a seat is vacant, the Government which appointed that member shall appoint another member in his place. A temporary member appointed under this subarticle shall continue to act until the substantive member resumes office, a person is appointed to fill the vacancy, or the matter is concluded. (3) Every question requiring a decision of the Special Constitutional Court shall be determined by the concurrence of two-thirds of the members from Mainland Tanzania and two-thirds of the members from Tanzania Zanzibar. (4) Parliament may enact a law prescribing the procedure for electing the Chairman of the Special Constitutional Court, bringing matters before the Court, conducting proceedings and communicating decisions to the Governments; provided that where a matter is brought before the Court when no such law exists, the matter shall be heard and determined according to a procedure prescribed by the Court before hearing begins, or, if the members fail to agree on that procedure, according to a procedure determined jointly by the Government of the United Republic and the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar.
vifungu: (1) The Special Constitutional Court shall sit only when there is a matter to be heard and shall hold its sittings at such place as may be determined in accordance with the procedure applicable to matters before the Court.

(2) The quorum at every sitting of the Special Constitutional Court shall be all its members; where any member is absent or a seat is vacant, the Government which appointed that member shall appoint another member in his place. A temporary member appointed under this subarticle shall continue to act until the substantive member resumes office, a person is appointed to fill the vacancy, or the matter is concluded.

(3) Every question requiring a decision of the Special Constitutional Court shall be determined by the concurrence of two-thirds of the members from Mainland Tanzania and two-thirds of the members from Tanzania Zanzibar.

(4) Parliament may enact a law prescribing the procedure for electing the Chairman of the Special Constitutional Court, bringing matters before the Court, conducting proceedings and communicating decisions to the Governments; provided that where a matter is brought before the Court when no such law exists, the matter shall be heard and determined according to a procedure prescribed by the Court before hearing begins, or, if the members fail to agree on that procedure, according to a procedure determined jointly by the Government of the United Republic and the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar.
